title: Source snapshot
description: The provenance record a fetcher writes into cli/data/<source>/SNAPSHOT.json. It is what makes 'regenerate the cards from source' a checkable claim rather than an aspiration: it names the upstream, pins ONE immutable release, and checksums the bytes taken from it. A source with no snapshot cannot be rebuilt, and facts derived from it carry no release.

source.description: The source name used in facts.source. Must match exactly, or the pin attaches to nothing.

upstream.description: The URL the fetcher read. A landing page for a versioned deposit is fine; an undated 'latest' file URL is not a pin and must be reflected by pin:null.

license.description: The licence the UPSTREAM declares, verbatim (SPDX id where the upstream gives one). Never our reading of it — that lives in the licence register, which this evidences.

citation.description: How the upstream asks to be cited.

pin.description: The immutable release identifier. NULL means this source could not be pinned — which is a real state and must not be faked. Downstream, no pin means no source_release row, which means every fact from it is flagged not-yet-regenerable.

kind.description: doi = a versioned DOI (strongest). commit = a git SHA. release = a publisher's dated/named release. version = a declared version string with nothing stronger behind it.

date.description: When the PUBLISHER released it. Not when we fetched it — that is fetchedAt, and conflating the two misdates our own provenance.

files.description: Every file this snapshot vouches for. Anything in the directory not listed here is unaccounted for.

sha256.description: Computed by us on retrieval. Proves the file has not changed since; does NOT by itself prove it is what the publisher shipped.

upstreamChecksum.description: The publisher's own checksum, '<algo>:<hex>'. Null where the publisher provides none (SIL, for instance).

upstreamVerified.description: True ONLY when upstreamChecksum was present AND matched the bytes on disk. This is the difference between provenance and assumption: a matching publisher checksum is proof the local file IS the named release; a plausible filename is not.

derivedFrom.description: For a file extracted from a verified archive: the archive it came out of. This is how a CSV inherits a DOI's authority legibly — the CSV's own hash is ours, but it came from bytes the publisher vouched for. Without this the chain would have to be assumed.

verified.description: Whether this snapshot's pin is trustworthy. Must be false whenever pin is null — a snapshot cannot be verified against no particular release.

fetchedBy.description: Path of the fetcher that wrote this.
